info.title: Pavement Conditions API
info.description:
The Pavement Conditions API v2 offers users pavement temperature and condition details for road segments in a specified area with enhanced GeoJSON support and pagination. DTN supplies road data on segments across North America and Europe, allowing users to request data for a geographic area or specific roadway within the database.

**What's New in v2.0.2:**
- Route Generation 
  
  — A new `GET /v2/directions` endpoint generates route geometry via the Mapbox Directions API.

- Query Pavement Conditions Along a Route or Route-Based Filtering (RB Filter)

  - Pavement data can be filtered using either `startPoint` and `endPoint` coordinates or a GeoJSON geometry provided in the request body.
  - When `startPoint` and `endPoint` are supplied to the `v2/logistics` or `v2/pavement/conditions` endpoints, a route is automatically generated internally via the Mapbox API.
  - Pagination is determined by the number of route `segments` when RB Filter is active.
  - Each paginated response includes a `statistics` object summarizing covered, uncovered, and total segment counts.
  - Results may be optionally narrowed by a weather `parameter` filter.
  - Results may also be optionally narrowed by Estimated Time of Arrival (`etaFilter`).

- Added pavementValidEndTime in returned data

**Authentication**: This API uses Bearer token authentication. When obtaining your access token, use the following audience values:
- **Production**: `https://pavement-condition.prd.wx.zones.dtn.com`
- **Staging**: `https://pavement-condition.stg.wx.zones.dtn.com`

Retrieves parameter details for v2 API. If the `name` query parameter is empty, it returns all parameters.
**v2 includes pagination parameters**: total, limit, page, nextOffset

| Variable Name | Description | Imperial Unit | Metric Unit |
| ------------- | ----------- | ------------- | ----------- |
| total | Total number of records available inside the BBox | N/A | N/A |
| limit | Maximum number of records per page | N/A | N/A |
| page | Current page number | N/A | N/A |
| nextOffset | Offset for the next page of results | N/A | N/A |
| id | Database table primary key ID | N/A | N/A |
| segmentId | Road segment identifier (string) | N/A | N/A |
| lat | Latitude for center point of road segment | Degrees | Degrees |
| lon | Longitude for center point of road segment | Degrees | Degrees |
| timestamp | Date/time for when the output variables are valid (UTC) - Use this for assigning time to the output | N/A | N/A |
| pavementCreationTime | Date/time when the pavement model was run (UTC) | N/A | N/A |
| pavementValidTime | Date/time for when the output variables are valid (UTC) | N/A | N/A |
| pavementValidEndTime | Date/time for when the pavement forecast validity period ends (UTC) | N/A | N/A |
| airTemp | Air temperature | Fahrenheit | Celsius |
| visibility | Visibility distance | mi | km |
| windDirection | Wind direction relative to true North (range from 0 to 360) | Degrees | Degrees |
| windGust | Wind gust speed | mi/hr | km/hr |
| windSpeed | Wind speed | mi/hr | km/hr |
| iceRate | Ice precipitation rate | in/hr | mm/hr |
| liquidRate | Liquid precipitation rate | in/hr | mm/hr |
| snowRate | Snow precipitation rate | in/hr | mm/hr |
| mobilityIndex | Mobility of vehicles compared to expected traffic patterns (100% mobility means traffic movement is expected to be unaffected by the conditions) - Same as in MDSS | Percent | Percent |
| pavementTemperature | Temperature of the road surface | Fahrenheit | Celsius |
| blowingSnowAlertLevel | Level of blowing snow intensity (2 - Lowest, 5 - Highest) | N/A | N/A |
| compactedSnowDepth | Depth of compacted snow on the road | in | mm |
| frostDepth | Depth of frost on the road | in | mm |
| iceDepth | Depth of ice on the road | in | mm |
| liquidDepth | Depth of liquid on the road | in | mm |
| snowDepth | Depth of snow on the road | in | mm |
| unbondedIceDepth | Depth of ice on the road that is not bonded to the road surface | in | mm |
| pavementCondition | Classification of the road condition. Possible conditions are dry, slush, chemical_wet, damp, wet, frost, ice, snow, compacted_snow - Same as in MDSS | N/A | N/A |

get.description:
Retrieves pavement conditions for road segments in GeoJSON FeatureCollection format. Returns up to 1000 records by default.
Data is grouped by segment ID with pagination metadata included in the response.

**Query modes:**
- By bounding box (`bbox`) — returns all segments within the area
- By route (`startPoint` + `endPoint`) — uses Mapbox Directions API to generate a route, then returns segments along it

**Filtering options:**
- Pavement data can be filtered using either `startPoint` and `endPoint` coordinates or a bounding box (`bbox`).
  - Results may be optionally narrowed by a weather `parameter` filter.
  - Results may also be optionally narrowed by Estimated Time of Arrival (`etaFilter`).

**Return Data:**

| Field Name | Description | Imperial Unit | Metric Unit |
| ---------- | ----------- | ------------- | ----------- |
| id | Database table primary key ID | N/A | N/A |
| segmentId | Road segment identifier (string) | N/A | N/A |
| lat | Latitude for center point of road segment | Degrees | Degrees |
| lon | Longitude for center point of road segment | Degrees | Degrees |
| timestamp | Date/time for when the output variables are valid (UTC) | N/A | N/A |
| pavementCreationTime | Date/time when the pavement model was run (UTC) | N/A | N/A |
| pavementValidTime | Date/time for when the output variables are valid (UTC) | N/A | N/A |
| pavementValidEndTime | Date/time for when the pavement forecast validity period ends (UTC) | N/A | N/A |
| airTemp | Air temperature | Fahrenheit | Celsius |
| visibility | Visibility distance | mi | km |
| windDirection | Wind direction relative to true North (range from 0 to 360) | Degrees | Degrees |
| windGust | Wind gust speed | mi/hr | km/hr |
| windSpeed | Wind speed | mi/hr | km/hr |
| iceRate | Ice precipitation rate | in/hr | mm/hr |
| liquidRate | Liquid precipitation rate | in/hr | mm/hr |
| snowRate | Snow precipitation rate | in/hr | mm/hr |
| mobilityIndex | Mobility of vehicles compared to expected traffic patterns (100% mobility means traffic movement is expected to be unaffected by the conditions) | Percent | Percent |
| pavementTemperature | Temperature of the road surface | Fahrenheit | Celsius |
| blowingSnowAlertLevel | Level of blowing snow intensity (2 - Lowest, 5 - Highest) | N/A | N/A |
| compactedSnowDepth | Depth of compacted snow on the road | in | mm |
| frostDepth | Depth of frost on the road | in | mm |
| iceDepth | Depth of ice on the road | in | mm |
| liquidDepth | Depth of liquid on the road | in | mm |
| snowDepth | Depth of snow on the road | in | mm |
| unbondedIceDepth | Depth of ice on the road that is not bonded to the road surface | in | mm |
| pavementCondition | Classification of the road condition. Possible conditions are dry, slush, chemical_wet, damp, wet, frost, ice, snow, compacted_snow | N/A | N/A |
| crashRiskIndex | Crash risk factor compared to average conditions (ex: 2.0 means the risk of crash is two times the average) | N/A | N/A |
| crashRiskUncertainty | One standard deviation on the crash risk factor (statistical error) | N/A | N/A |
| roadName | Name of the road or highway | N/A | N/A |
| osmClass | OpenStreetMap road classification (e.g., motorway, trunk, primary) | N/A | N/A |
| geometry | GeoJSON geometry representing the road segment (LineString or MultiLineString) | N/A | N/A |
| createdAt | Record creation timestamp | N/A | N/A |
| updatedAt | Record last update timestamp | N/A | N/A |

**Sample Requests:**

1. **Get default data (1000 records):**
   ```
   GET /v2/pavement/conditions
   ```

2. **Get data for specific geographic area (US):**
   ```
   GET /v2/pavement/conditions?bbox=-156.1317111,19.6270521,-155.9317111,19.8270521
   ```

3. **Get data for European area:**
   ```
   GET /v2/pavement/conditions?bbox=3.555,49.470,6.262,50.849
   ```

4. **Get specific page:**
   ```
   GET /v2/pavement/conditions?bbox=-156.1317111,19.6270521,-155.9317111,19.8270521&limit=1000&page=2
   ```

5. **Filter by time range:**
   ```
   GET /v2/pavement/conditions?bbox=-156.1317111,19.6270521,-155.9317111,19.8270521&startTime=2025-12-04T20:00:00.000Z&endTime=2025-12-05T20:00:00.000Z
   ```

6. **Get data in metric units:**
   ```
   GET /v2/pavement/conditions?units=metric
   ```

7. **Route-based filtering with departure time:**
   ```
   GET /v2/pavement/conditions?startPoint=-93.3905,45.1310&endPoint=-93.2695,45.1420&departAt=2026-03-13T15:00:00.000Z
   ```

8. **Route-based filtering with arrival time:**
   ```
   GET /v2/pavement/conditions?startPoint=-93.3905,45.1310&endPoint=-93.2695,45.1420&arriveAt=2026-03-13T16:00:00.000Z
   ```

9. **Route-based with ETA filter (single forecast per segment):**
   ```
   GET /v2/pavement/conditions?startPoint=-93.3905,45.1310&endPoint=-93.2695,45.1420&departAt=2026-03-13T15:00:00.000Z&etaFilter=true
   ```

10. **Route-based with parameter filter:**
    ```
    GET /v2/pavement/conditions?startPoint=-93.3905,45.1310&endPoint=-93.2695,45.1420&departAt=2026-03-13T15:00:00.000Z&parameter=crashRiskIndex,mobilityIndex
    ```

post.description:
Retrieves pavement conditions along a route in GeoJSON FeatureCollection format.
Supports two modes:

**Option 1 - Mapbox waypoints (query params):**
Provide `startPoint` and `endPoint` to automatically generate a route via Mapbox Directions API.
Optionally provide `departAt` or `arriveAt` (mutually exclusive) for per-segment timing.

**Option 2 - Direct route (body):**
Provide a GeoJSON LineString or FeatureCollection in the request body.

**Filtering options:**
- Pavement data can be filtered using either `startPoint` and `endPoint` coordinates or a GeoJSON geometry provided in the request body.
  - Results may be optionally narrowed by a weather `parameter` filter.
  - Results may also be optionally narrowed by Estimated Time of Arrival (`etaFilter`).

Query parameters take priority over the request body when both are provided.

**Timing behavior:**
- When `departAt` is provided: each feature includes `arrivalTime` and the response includes `properties.arrivalTimeUTC` (departAt + route duration)
- When `arriveAt` is provided: each feature includes `departureTime` and the response includes `properties.departureTimeUTC` (arriveAt - route duration)

**Sample Requests:**

1. **Route via Mapbox with departure time:**
   ```
   POST /v2/pavement/conditions?startPoint=-93.3905,45.1310&endPoint=-93.2695,45.1420&departAt=2026-03-13T15:00:00.000Z
   ```

2. **Route via Mapbox with arrival time:**
   ```
   POST /v2/pavement/conditions?startPoint=-93.3905,45.1310&endPoint=-93.2695,45.1420&arriveAt=2026-03-13T16:00:00.000Z
   ```

3. **Direct route via body:**
   ```
   POST /v2/pavement/conditions
   Body: { "type": "LineString", "coordinates": [[-93.39, 45.13], [-93.27, 45.14]] }
   ```

get.description:
Returns cacheable route geometry from the Mapbox Directions API as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection.
This endpoint decouples route geometry from weather/pavement data, enabling independent caching
of the route so the frontend can lock in a stable geometry for navigation (similar to Waze/Google Maps).

The `geojson` field in the response is directly compatible with the POST `/v2/pavement/conditions`
and POST `/v2/logistics` endpoints — it can be passed as the `route` body without transformation.

**Timing behavior:**
- When `departAt` is provided: each feature includes `arrivalTimeUTC` (departAt + route duration)
- When `arriveAt` is provided: each feature includes `departureTimeUTC` (arriveAt - route duration)
- When neither is provided: current server time is used as `departAt` and `arrivalTimeUTC` is computed

**Alternative routes:**
- When `alternatives=true`: returns 1–3 routes sorted by ascending duration
- When `alternatives=false` or omitted: returns exactly 1 route

**Sample Requests:**

1. **Basic route with departure time:**
   ```
   GET /v2/directions?startPoint=-93.3905,45.1310&endPoint=-93.2695,45.1420&departAt=2026-03-13T15:00:00.000Z
   ```

2. **Route with arrival time:**
   ```
   GET /v2/directions?startPoint=-93.3905,45.1310&endPoint=-93.2695,45.1420&arriveAt=2026-03-13T16:00:00.000Z
   ```

3. **Multiple alternative routes:**
   ```
   GET /v2/directions?startPoint=-93.3905,45.1310&endPoint=-93.2695,45.1420&departAt=2026-03-13T15:00:00.000Z&alternatives=true
   ```

4. **Default timing (uses current server time as departure):**
   ```
   GET /v2/directions?startPoint=-93.3905,45.1310&endPoint=-93.2695,45.1420
   ```

parameters.name: startPoint
parameters.description:
Starting point coordinates for the route.
Format: `longitude,latitude`

parameters.name: endPoint
parameters.description:
Ending point coordinates for the route.
Format: `longitude,latitude`

parameters.name: departAt
parameters.description:
Departure time for the route. Mutually exclusive with `arriveAt`.
When provided, `arrivalTimeUTC` is calculated as `departAt + route duration`.
Format: ISO 8601 UTC with "Z" suffix (e.g., 2026-03-13T15:00:00Z)

parameters.name: arriveAt
parameters.description:
Desired arrival time at the destination. Mutually exclusive with `departAt`.
When provided, `departureTimeUTC` is calculated as `arriveAt - route duration`.
Format: ISO 8601 UTC with "Z" suffix (e.g., 2026-03-13T16:00:00Z)

parameters.name: alternatives
parameters.description:
When "true", returns up to 3 alternative routes sorted by ascending duration.
When "false" or omitted, returns exactly 1 route.

clientCredentials.description:
# Using DAIS for M2M/API Auth
You have been given a Client ID and a Client Secret, which are used to request a DTN Access Token. DTN Access Tokens are required when making calls to each and every DTN API endpoint. The following information provides additional details on these tokens and how they are generated.
## What is an Access Token and how is it different from an API Key?
An API Key is a random string of characters that an API uses to authorize whether or not a calling client has approved access to an endpoint. These keys are a non-standard approach to API authorization and are generally issued on a per-API basis.

An Access Token is also a string of characters but is a base-64 encoded JavaScript Object Notation Web Token, or JWT. JWTs are a widely accepted standard that use OAuth concepts and approaches. 

Both API Keys and Access Tokens are used in an Authorization Request Header as a Bearer, meaning there is no difference in where you put this string of characters when you make calls to DTN APIs.
## How to generate an Access Token?
When requested, an Access Token is generated for your specific Client (ID/Secret) and for a specific API. The DTN Auth and Identity Service (DAIS) generates new Access Tokens for your client. The DAIS endpoint is `POST https://api.auth.dtn.com/v1/tokens/authorize`.

This endpoint takes two Header parameters:
  * `Content-Type: application/json`
  * `Accept: application/json`

This endpoint takes four parameters in the Request Body:
  * `grant_type`: this should always be client_credentials for generating machine-to-machine tokens.
  * `client_id`: this is the Client ID or Application ID using the token and is given to you by DTN's Identity Team. This ID will never change for your client/application.
  * `client_secret`: this is the Client Secret that is associated with the Application ID and is given to you by DTN's Identity Team. This key is subject to rotation for security purposes but always with the client's knowledge.
  * `audience`: this is the API for which this Access Token will be used. For the DTN Pavement Conditions API, you need to use the following audience: https://pavement-condition.prd.wx.zones.dtn.com

You can use this CURL command template as a reference for obtaining an access token:
  ```
  curl --location --request POST 'https://api.auth.dtn.com/v1/tokens/authorize' \
--header 'Accept: application/json' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '{
"grant_type": "client_credentials",
"client_id": "insert your client id here",
"client_secret": "insert your client secret here",
"audience": "insert your audience here"
}' 
  ```

*This document, for demonstration purposes, supplies a client_id and client_secret in all code examples. This client/application is for a fictitious API and cannot be used in practice to gain unauthorized access to any other DTN API.*
Upon generating a new Access Token, you should receive an HTTP Response from DAIS similar to this:
  ```
  {
    "data": {
          "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCIsImtpZCI6InpfX21pZW13NGhoTmdvQWQxR3N6ciJ9..0VHdyp1w9PPFVI0FPheAwuKZwb5C25rwP-LPMXcSNoRmouvga1DZtNLA67ZzE_sAlc_VpaDRr6daLKr_Alw4347mw9sdjP8wKR27kCZa9JZK5PGQMmXHscATbzBEJYpCPklfyGaajgymqTBGnedcv8F0UvlRzQPsFeRPnVoX7BWOSXpMbyToGiXWkQLBQT7r96KAmLZOPJFZspPtjw-wH2mSL2WNa_nkB4j5vMGhGxlKiNRsKb30TH_WAel2hsxNlcPK3XHCmrMTYsNnu7HNqOTMn2i0__0rvBrhSWEw-_grqQDmWFJuWd7Qhi1q81AaJcdqgoSa_efz93QFclJUNw",
          "scope": "read:demo create:demo update:demo",
          "expires_in": 90,
          "token_type": "Bearer"
      },
      "meta": {
          "date_time": "2022-06-24T19:09:42.963Z",
          "name": "v1.tokens.authorize",
          "uuid": "ee6f9feb-dcf8-4421-a6fd-efd6beabdaa9",
          "start_timestamp": 1656097782509,
          "end_timestamp": 1656097782963,
          "execution_time": 454
      }
  }
  ```
Looking at this Response, you will see:
  * `access_token`: contains the JWT Access Token string you will use as your Bearer token.
  * `scope`: contains the scopes that this Access Token gives you permissions to access.
  * `expires_in`: contains the length of time before this Access Token will expire, in seconds.
  * `token_type`: verifies that this Access Token should be used as a Bearer token.

## How to use an Access Token after one is generated?
Once a new Access Token is obtained, it is used in each call to a DTN API endpoint as a Bearer token in an Authorization Request Header. For example:
  ```
  Header: 'Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCIsImtpZCI6InpfX21pZW13NGhoTmdvQWQxR3N6ciJ9..0VHdyp1w9PPFVI0FPheAwuKZwb5C25rwP-LPMXcSNoRmouvga1DZtNLA67ZzE_sAlc_VpaDRr6daLKr_Alw4347mw9sdjP8wKR27kCZa9JZK5PGQMmXHscATbzBEJYpCPklfyGaajgymqTBGnedcv8F0UvlRzQPsFeRPnVoX7BWOSXpMbyToGiXWkQLBQT7r96KAmLZOPJFZspPtjw-wH2mSL2WNa_nkB4j5vMGhGxlKiNRsKb30TH_WAel2hsxNlcPK3XHCmrMTYsNnu7HNqOTMn2i0__0rvBrhSWEw-_grqQDmWFJuWd7Qhi1q81AaJcdqgoSa_efz93QFclJUNw'
  ```

## Deconstructing the Access Token
A DTN Access Token carries information within its JWT Body that is available on every API call. By deconstructing the JWT token, our Access Tokens will resemble:
  ```
  {
    "https://auth.dtn.com/customerId": "1234567890Demo",
    "https://auth.dtn.com/productCode": "DemoApiP",
    "https://auth.dtn.com/requesterIp": "18.213.174.27",
    "https://auth.dtn.com/rps": "100",
    "https://auth.dtn.com/tier": "Basic",
    "https://auth.dtn.com/quota": "999999",
    "iss": "https://id.auth.dtn.com/",
    "sub": "nfyO3KiKPR8N0DKR5CL8jS9GFBCDeyFM@clients",
    "aud": "https://demo-api.auth.dtn.com/",
    "iat": 1656099068,
    "exp": 1656099158,
    "azp": "nfyO3KiKPR8N0DKR5CL8jS9GFBCDeyFM",
    "scope": "read:demo create:demo update:demo",
    "gty": "client-credentials",
    "permissions": [
      "read:demo",
      "create:demo",
      "update:demo"
    ]
  }
  ```
### Description of Claims

  | Claim                              | Type                                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
  | -----------------------------------| --------------------------------------------| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/customerId`  | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the Customer ID found in the DTN Order Management/Salesforce system associated with this token.                                                                                                |
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/productCode` | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the Identity product code associated with this token.                                                                                                                                          |
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/requesterIp` | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the IP address of the requesting client.                                                                                                                                                       |
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/rps`         | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the maximum rate per second this customer is authorized to utilize.                                                                                                                            |
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/tier`        | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the data tier the customer purchased for the requested access.                                                                                                                                 |
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/quota`       | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the maximum yearly quota the customer purchased for calling DTN endpoints for the specific product.                                                                                            |
  | `iss`                              | String (URI)                                | The Security Token Service (STS) that issues and returns the token. If this value is not from `https://id.auth.dtn.com/`, the token should not be considered trusted.                                                      |
  | `sub`                              | String (URI)                                | The principle about which the token asserts information (the User ID or Client ID within the Identity Provider). A User ID will start with a prefix of `auth0\|`, while the Client ID will end with the suffix `@clients`. |
  | `aud`                              | String \| Array (Strings) (URI \| [URI, …]) | Identifies the intended recipient(s) of the token – its audience. The token should be rejected if the audience does not contain values expected by the calling application.                                                |
  | `iat`                              | Number (Timestamp)                          | “Issued At” indicates when the authentication for this token occurred.                                                                                                                                                     |
  | `exp`                              | Number (Timestamp)                          | The “expiration time” on or after which the JWT must not be accepted for processing.                                                                                                                                       |
  | `azp`                              | String                                      | The application/client ID of the client using the token. The application can cat as itself or on behalf of a user.                                                                                                         |
  | `gty`                              | String (Space-delimited)                    | The grant type that was used to request the token – not an RFC 7519 registered claim (Auth0-specific).                                                                                                                     |
  | `permissions`                      | Array (Strings)                             | The grant type that was used to request the token – not an RFC 7519 registered claim (Auth0-specific).                                                                                                                     |
